transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to convene the capital-return review on the potential share repurchase the board has authorized us to consider. As you know, the board has given us latitude to repurchase up to 5,000,000 shares this quarter, and our stock is currently trading near $8.25. Before I finalize any authorization, I need input from each of your areas. Treasury — I'd like your assessment of liquidity and cash position. Legal and compliance — I need your read on regulatory requirements and any constraints on execution method. Investor relations — please give me your view on how the market and our shareholders would interpret a repurchase at this time. Let's work through this systematically.

transcript.text: Good morning, Maya. On the treasury side, I want to flag a key constraint. My cash forecast was confirmed this morning after a scheduled tax payment was added, and it supports a maximum repurchase consideration of exactly $32,000,000 while preserving our treasury liquidity floor. I should note that this $32,000,000 is the treasury spending-cap ceiling to record in the authorization — it's not a computed consideration from multiplying offer shares by an offer price. This forecast has not yet been circulated with the board materials, so I want to make sure everyone here has this figure as we work through the review.

transcript.text: Maya, before we go further on execution method and offer size, I need to flag a constraint I found this week while reviewing the equity records. Of the 5,000,000 shares the board authorized us to consider repurchasing, 1,200,000 are held in the employee benefit trust and cannot be purchased in this offer. That means the executable offer size is exactly 3,800,000 shares. I have not yet updated the transaction checklist to reflect this, but everyone should be working from 3,800,000 as the maximum number of shares we can actually acquire.

transcript.text: Maya, on the investor relations front, I need to share something important. This morning I received a written indication from our largest institutional holder. They've stated they will participate only in a fixed-price offer at exactly 825 cents per share — that's $8.25 — rather than an open-market buyback. This indication is still in my investor-relations file and hasn't been shared with the rest of the group yet. I think this is a critical data point as we consider execution method and pricing, especially given the constraints treasury and legal have already raised.
